kind: Warped current cones and continuous endpoint equations independently reconstructed
scope: Two directly reconstructed warped-current cone and continuous finite-endpoint equation proofs, including the obstruction to global C11 solutions.
mathematical_boundary: The fixed warped product and finite disjoint power-stratum regime only. No general P15 closure, endpoint potential uniqueness/selection, whole-family convergence, classical smoothness off the extreme set or pointwise convergence of minimizing balanced metrics.

mathematics.method: Direct reconstruction from exact previously retained book inputs; no automatic theorem verdict

obligations.claim: The fixed product has dimension n=m+1 with m>=2.
The base and curve volume integrals are normalized to one.
The reference h=kappa+w is a smooth strictly positive metric.
The cone parameters b,c,e are arbitrary real numbers.
Nonconstancy of a makes the three original span directions independent modulo smooth dd^c.
Distributional Stokes is valid for arbitrary global quasi-plurisubharmonic potentials against closed smooth tests.
The horizontal test kappa^(m-1) wedge w is closed and semipositive.
Its pairing forces b>=delta with the exact unit normalization.
Every smooth nonnegative base top-degree form pulls back to a closed semipositive test.
Horizontal terms wedge that top-degree form to zero by dimension.
The curve integral is one, so the vertical pairing is exactly integral_B (L-delta) eta.
An open set with L<delta admits a nonzero nonnegative supported test.
The localized inequality forces L>=delta everywhere.
The extrema zero and M reduce L>=0 to e>=0 and e+cM>=0.
The nonnegative parameter inequalities make theta semipositive, supplying the zero-potential current.
Semipositivity makes every theta+epsilon h strictly positive.
Nef smooth representative tests conversely give the same nonnegative limits.
A strict current lower bound forces b>0 and both extreme L-values positive.
Those strict inequalities make theta itself uniformly positive by compactness.
No singular potential is restricted to an extreme fiber.
Every finite face has b>0 and the relevant ratio r>1.
Scaling M-a to 1-a/M preserves the codimension/order ratio.
The endpoint L_0 is a positive constant multiple of its nonnegative extreme function.
Tubular Jacobians and the power-stratum bounds reduce Lp integrability to codimension>k_i p.
A common 1<p<r works on every one of the finitely many extreme tubes.
The function is bounded below away from those tubes.
Positive codimension makes the union of extreme strata have zero smooth volume.
The density can be assigned a finite value there without changing its measure.
Both face coefficient formulas give H_0=n b^m.
The previously proved continuous Lp existence applies to the positive closed base background b kappa.
Its equation normalization scalar is lambda, distinct from the fixed real cone parameter c.
The bounded closed mass identity fixes lambda=b^m/H_0.
The holomorphic projection pulls back a continuous quasi-plurisubharmonic potential.
The resulting A+L_0 w is globally positive.
Bounded products commute with this holomorphic submersion.
The (m+1)-st power of the pulled-back base current vanishes.
The square of the smooth vertical form L_0 w vanishes.
Multilinearity leaves only the binomial term n L_0 A^m wedge w.
Absolute continuity and zero volume of the extreme set justify L_0 times sigma/L_0=sigma globally as measures.
The unit normalization makes the final product exactly the smooth probability mu.
A global C11 potential has uniformly bounded measurable complex Hessian coefficients.
The C11 product theorem identifies its top product with the almost-everywhere determinant.
The smooth positive ratio mu/h^n has a positive lower bound on the compact product.
An upper eigenvalue bound and a positive determinant lower bound give a lower bound for every eigenvalue.
The almost-everywhere bound gives the strict current inequality distributionally.
The strict-current cone excludes that inequality because L_0 vanishes.
The obstruction applies to every solution, without a pullback premise.
